newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: CRICKET-STEWART, GOUGH PUT ENGLAND IN COMMAND.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-STEWART, GOUGH PUT ENGLAND IN COMMAND.

text.p: England had built a commanding position at tea on the second day of the second test against New Zealand at the Basin Reserve on Friday.
Led by a fired-up Darren Gough, England scuttled New Zealand for 124 in the morning and then batted solidly on a lively wicket to reach 115 for three wickets at tea.
England's innings was built around form batsman Alec Stewart, who appeared to be on his way to a third century in as many tests and in successive innings.
However, just before tea he fell to a brilliant diving left- handed catch by Stephen Fleming at first slip off left-armer Geoff Allott for 52.
At the interval Nasser Hussain was on 14 and Graham Thorpe was on five.
After losing Nick Knight with the score on 10 before lunch Stewart and captain Mike Atherton set about overhauling New Zealand's modest score.
The pair put on 70 in just over even time and despite the bowlers still being able to extract considerable movement and lift, were able to drive with freedom at times.
Atherton looked well set on 30, having just imperiously off- driven Simon Doull to the boundary when the seam bowler had him trapped leg before playing forward.
Stewart, who scored 101 not out in the second test against Zimbabwe and 173 in the first test in Auckland, reached his 50 in 76 balls and hit six boundaries.
He bought up his half century with a savage on-drive from Doull and earlier hit 10 off the same bowler included two sweetly timed drives.
In the morning session, New Zealand resuming at 56 for six, offered some resistance via Nathan Astle (36) and Dipak Patel (45), but Gough, Andrew Caddick and Dominic Cork completed the rout.
The aggressive Gough ended with five for 40 off 16 overs, his second five-wicket test bag.
New Zealand-raised Andy Caddick, in a return to test cricket, did the kiwis no favours, finishing with four for 45.
